answer: A concrete Sybil defense is mandatory bonding tied to a reusable identity. Each new agent locks a bond and solves a verifiable memory-hard puzzle. Honest agents recover their stake after a healthy term, so the cost is delay, not loss. An attacker forging a thousand identities pays that flat price a thousand times: bonds are slashed and work wasted once collusion is found. Like a prism, one credential cannot refract into many, and each fake voyage from a fresh identity restarts the costly climb. Where a cheap pigment of reputation lets clones blend in, a bond makes them stand out.
